story: At 11:17 on a sunny Sunday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is in his garage wiring lights and speakers to his golf cart battery and checking every mount, determined to keep the whole setup tucked safely inside. Donna is busy hauling extra flamingos behind the hedge so that only three stand in view along Magnolia Loop, and Hal is heading down the street to see how the decorating is going. Rosa, patient and hopeful, sips her coffee on her porch, keeping an eye out for Hal while she works out a friendly way to remind the neighbors about the November 7 Halloween decor deadline without sounding like the HOA.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Power up the lights and speakers off the cart battery, check every connection and mount, keep it all inside the garage
Donna (donna flamingo flock): Carry the extra flamingos behind the hedge, leaving exactly three visible from the street
Hal headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Rosa waited: Sip my coffee on the porch, keep an eye on the walk for Hal, and think through how to mention the November 7 Halloween decor deadline to the neighbors without sounding like the HOA.

gary.thought_process: Brackets are mounted and the tested light harness and speaker leads are run, all inside the garage. The parade is rolling, the holiday lighting window under L-04 doesn't open until Thanksgiving, and exterior cart mods visible from the street need Architectural Review approval under L-01. So I shouldn't roll this out on the street yet. The sensible next step is to power it up in the garage, check that every light strip and speaker is secure and working off the cart battery, and keep the volume sensible. After that I'll need to deal with the review paperwork at Town Hall. Staying busy on this feels good, and it keeps the house from being too quiet.

parameters.content: Power up the lights and speakers off the cart battery, check every connection and mount, keep it all inside the garage

donna.thought_process: I've been trying to pull the extra flamingos behind the hedge for a few ticks now, and the street is still the place to do it. I promised Hal I'd thin the flock to exactly three visible before parade day. Nobody's around, so I'll just get it done and stop dithering. Then I can go find Gary for another round of drills.

parameters.content: Carry the extra flamingos behind the hedge, leaving exactly three visible from the street

hal.thought_process: I've been scanning and updating that notebook for days, and from my porch I can't even see a neighbor in range. Notebooks don't file themselves. The architectural review committee needs a clean report on Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos, and Magnolia Loop is where the evidence stands. A proper count with my own eyes, up close, beats binoculars. Donna's promise to thin the flock before parade day still needs checking, and the parade's come and gone. Rosa's coffee is tomorrow, so today I do my duty and get some air. Order and respect, one street at a time.

parameters.content: Heading out to Magnolia Loop to do a proper on-the-ground count of Donna's flamingos and look over Gary's cart modifications.

rosa.thought_process: It's 11:17 and Hal still isn't on my walk. I've already poured coffee, set out mugs and pastries, and checked my schedule, so there's nothing left to prep. Nobody is in line-of-sight to speak to, and I don't want to wander off and miss him when he arrives. The pastries and coffee are on the table, so the best move is to keep waiting on the porch, enjoy the sunny morning, and rehearse how I'll bring up the November 7 Halloween decor deadline gently with Hal, then pass it along to Gary and Donna.

parameters.content: Sip my coffee on the porch, keep an eye on the walk for Hal, and think through how to mention the November 7 Halloween decor deadline to the neighbors without sounding like the HOA.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
